scenario: Actual Insiders Agents Window; synthetic multiple-choice question waiting unanswered. No terminal command or active model generation in the measured state.

method.order: Alternating active/baseline and baseline/active within each case
method.cpuScope: Sum of renderer CPU time in the isolated native instance; percentage of one CPU core. GPU and browser process CPU recorded separately.
method.baseline: Both target animations static; native shimmer timeline driver stops scheduling further frame writes.
method.control: Original native animations retained. Logo Web Animation paused/played. Shimmer is frozen using playbackRate=0 and play(), so its native paused-animation driver exits; restored with native pause mode and the native animation-start event listener.
method.verification: Animation timeline deltas, shimmer driver currentTime writes, target identity/visibility, unchanged viewport and request content; no other running Web Animations.

thresholds.High: Every paired CPU delta >= 5 percentage points
thresholds.Low: Every delta strictly between -1 and +1 point

limitations: Single device, installed build, window size and synthetic waiting state; shared OS/background activity is not controlled.
Temporary runtime control is instrumentation, not a shipped user setting.
The targeted shimmer currentTime accessor counts writes identically in all conditions; its added overhead is not separately calibrated.
Renderer CPU excludes GPU process CPU; additional process scopes are reported separately.
This is CPU cost, not proof of user input slowdown, power consumption, or a universal hardware-independent rating.
Both-on CPU is measured separately; individual effects should not be added because rendering work can be shared.

shimmer.implementation: native CSS background-position animation with JS timeline driver
